Annual gross revenue. Based on trailing 12-month AirROI performance of 6 comparable properties. Occupancy is measured on open nights (nights booked ÷ nights open to guests); the comps' median is 365 open nights a year.

How occupancy is measured: the annual occupancy figures in this report are on open nights: nights booked divided by the nights the home was open to guests (AirROI excludes nights the owner blocked). Monthly and seasonal figures are AirROI's monthly occupancy. On that basis the comps booked 21% to 88% of their open nights over the last 12 months. In the summer rate-card season (Jun–Sep) they averaged 78% and from November to April 43%. In AirROI's data for this area, higher nightly rates come with lower occupancy: 22 of the 67 active lake homes in the search booked 40% or more of their open nights, and 1 of those averaged $1,000+ a night. AirROI's location estimate for a typical 4-bedroom home here is 43% occupancy at $585 a night.
How the base case is derived: We combine two independent AirROI methods: the median trailing-12-month revenue of the 6 comparable listings ($184,072) and AirROI's revenue estimate for a 4-bedroom, 4.5-bath, 10-guest home at this location ($90,992). The base case is the average of the two: $137,532. The two methods are 50.6% apart.

Compared with the current summer rate card: 81 Timberlane's published 16-week summer schedule totals $228,000 if every week sells. That works out to $2,036 per night across 112 nights. The rate card is $90,468 above the full-year comp-based base case. Based on the comp set's monthly AirROI revenue, 61% of annual revenue falls in Jun–Sep, about $83,318 of the base case. The rate card's nightly equivalent is 3.2x the base-case ADR ($638). Why the two differ: the rate card is an asking price that assumes 100% of summer weeks sell. The comps are what Airbnb listings actually earned over the last 12 months, including their unbooked nights. Weekly agency rentals like this one are not in AirROI's Airbnb data, so the comps may not reflect this property's own booking history. Use the rate card as the summer ceiling and the comp-based numbers as the year-round, nightly-rental view.

Methodology

Assumptions & Methodology

Comp selection
  • 4-7 bedrooms (subject has 4; larger homes are labeled), sleeps 7-13 (subject sleeps 10, plus or minus 3), waterfront, lake access or boat slip, rated 4.8+
  • AirROI radius search within 12 miles of the subject, entire homes only
  • Must list waterfront, lake access or a boat slip in AirROI's amenity data
  • Must have AirROI trailing-12-month revenue
  • At least 3 reviews, rated 4.8+
  • At least 30 nights booked in the last 12 months (an established, active listing)
  • Ranked by AirROI trailing-12-month revenue, highest first: these are the top-performing lake homes in the search, not the average home
Scenario math
  • Conservative: the lower of the comp 25th percentile and AirROI's location estimate for a typical home (when it is the estimate, it is shown with the estimate's own occupancy and ADR)
  • Base: average of the comp median and AirROI's location estimate
  • Optimistic: the highest of the comp 75th percentile, AirROI's 75th-percentile estimate and the base case
  • Occupancy is on open nights: AirROI nights booked ÷ nights open to guests (total days minus blocked days). Each scenario uses the matching comp percentile
  • ADR = revenue ÷ (occupancy × 365 open nights, the comp median)
Data sources
  • AirROI /listings/search/radius, /listings/metrics/all and /calculator/estimate: comp revenue, occupancy, ADR, availability, monthly performance and AirROI's location estimate
  • Published rate card: Published 2027 weekly rates, Yankee Pedlar (winnire.com)
  • Raw AirROI responses are saved alongside this report
